questions.question: Convex mirrors make cars look:
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give you a wider view of the road than flat mirrors. However, they make objects look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: Wearing which of the following will NOT help prevent serious injury?
questions.explanation: To protect yourself from injury, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high sturdy boots or shoes that cover your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: What can help if your drive chain slips?
questions.explanation: If your chain slips, try tightening it. If tightening does not fix the problem, replace the chain before riding again.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should ride near the front because:

options.text: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
They will get lost if they lead.
They may slow the group down as leaders.
They will ride too fast in any other spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can watch them easily.

questions.question: Which material gives the best protection to motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather provides the best protection for motorcycle riders. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs completely.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Either the front or rear brake, but not both.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Many over-the-counter drugs:

options.text: Only affect your riding if you drink alcohol too.
Have the same effect on every person.

questions.explanation: Many drugs, including over-the-counter medications, prescription medications, and illegal drugs, have side effects that can make it unsafe to ride.

questions.question: On a two-lane road, a group of riders should pass another vehicle:
questions.explanation: Pass one rider at a time. The second rider should wait until the first rider is safely back in the original lane before starting to pass. Continue this pattern until all riders have safely passed.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has an effect similar to:
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have manual transmissions. Downshifting to a lower gear slows you down.

questions.question: Your body can only remove alcohol through:
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.

questions.question: A face shield should:

options.text: Allow you to see clearly to both sides.
Block all air from passing through it.
Be tight enough so glasses cannot fit underneath.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow you to see clearly to both sides.
questions.explanation: A good face shield must have no scratches, resist penetration, allow clear views to both sides, fasten securely, let air pass through, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: Which of the following protects your eyes from the wind?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect a rider's eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not shield eyes well enough.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, ride on the left side of your lane because:

options.text: The right side could be slippery.
It gives you the best view of hazards in the next lane.
People don't usually expect to be passed on their left.
It puts you in the rearview mirror of the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you the best view of hazards in the next lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the left portion of your lane increases your line of sight and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If a dog chases you, you should:

options.text: Stop until the animal loses interest.
Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Dogs often chase motorcycles. Downshift and approach the dog slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: An experienced rider:

options.text: Changes position within their lane based on road conditions.
Stays in one part of the lane at all times.
Weaves within the lane to be more visible.
Travels only on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes position within their lane based on road conditions.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists have three lane position options. Choose the safest position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: To reduce crash risk, you should do all of the following except:

options.text: Be visible by wearing proper clothing and using your headlight.
Signal your intentions using turn signals and brake lights.
Search for hazards in your path.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to other drivers, signal your intentions, and keep space around you. Search for and identify hazards. Be ready to react to anything.

questions.question: When riding in a group and passing another vehicle, it is best to:

options.text: Allow one rider to fully pass before another rider starts to pass.
Allow several riders to pass at the same time.
Have the last rider wave to show no other motorcycles are coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow one rider to fully pass before another rider starts to pass.
questions.explanation: Group riders should pass one at a time. Each rider completes their pass and returns to formation before the next rider begins.

questions.question: If a dog chases you, you should:

options.text: Stop until the animal loses interest.
Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Downshift and slowly approach the dog. Once you are close, accelerate and leave it behind. Do not kick the dog.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking, you should do all of the following except:

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for your friend.
Involve your friend in activities to distract them from drinking.
Keep your friend from leaving until they are sober.
Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Prevent impaired riding by arranging another ride, involving them in activities, using any excuse to keep them from leaving before sober, and having other friends help intervene.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, you may need to:

options.text: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting safely.
Flash your brakes to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting safely.
questions.explanation: Before downshifting, slow to a safe speed. Downshifting too fast may cause the motorcycle to lurch and the rear wheel to skid. Use brakes to slow down before downshifting on downhill slopes or into first gear.

questions.question: How should you sit on a motorcycle to control it properly?

options.text: Sit so your arms steer the motorcycle, not hold you up.
Sit far back on the seat so your arms stay straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so your arms steer the motorcycle, not hold you up.
questions.explanation: Sit so you use your arms to steer, not to support your weight. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handlebars. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests to help with balance.

questions.question: Which is NOT required for effective eye or face shield protection?

options.text: It must be too tight to wear sunglasses or eyeglasses.
It must be free of scratches.
It must allow clear views to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: It must be too tight to wear sunglasses or eyeglasses.
questions.explanation: An effective eye or face shield must be free of scratches, fasten securely, allow clear side views, resist penetration, prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: Which sign is usually rectangular?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black lettering. Riders must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, what should you do?

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
Start slowing down later than usual.
Brake gently to avoid overworking the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger in a sidecar adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. You need more space and time to stop.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards.
